subject.title: fix(config): normalize MCP server disabled flag to enabled:false

question: Should OpenClaw officially accept `disabled` as a second user-facing MCP server enablement key despite the existing canonical `enabled` contract?
rationale: Adding a persistent config alias and precedence rule is a compatibility-sensitive product choice; the current repository policy and documented surface favor rejecting it or handling it only at a migration/import boundary.

options.title: Keep one canonical key
options.body: Reject the runtime alias and replace it, if useful, with validation or Doctor guidance directing users to `enabled: false`.

options.title: Sponsor the alias
options.body: Accept `disabled` only after aligning schema, CLI, UI, docs, deterministic key removal, precedence behavior, Doctor migration, and fresh/upgrade proof.

options.title: Close as unsupported input
options.body: Close this PR and the linked report with the existing `enabled: false` CLI and UI workflow as the supported solution.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical key
recommendation.body: Reject the runtime alias and replace it, if useful, with validation or Doctor guidance directing users to `enabled: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior work established the MCP canonicalization and Doctor-repair boundary affected by this decision.
